subject.title: Feature request: Mid-stream message injection (soft steer)

question: Should OpenClaw add true soft-steer semantics beyond current boundary steering, and if so should it be a new opt-in queue mode/policy or a change to existing steer behavior?
rationale: The requested behavior changes when active runs may be interrupted, how partial assistant output and tool results are preserved, and which session context receives injected input; current code and docs intentionally define boundary steering plus a separate interrupt mode.

options.title: Design opt-in soft steer
options.body: Define a new mode or policy for abort/capture/inject/resume semantics, with tests for streaming, tools, Codex turn/steer, fallback, and transcript state.

options.title: Keep boundary steering only
options.body: Close or narrow the broader soft-steer direction and use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/48003 for remaining boundary-steering ingress bugs.

options.title: Change steer globally
options.body: Make existing steer more aggressive by default, accepting compatibility risk for users who expect tool-boundary behavior.

recommendation.title: Design opt-in soft steer
recommendation.body: Define a new mode or policy for abort/capture/inject/resume semantics, with tests for streaming, tools, Codex turn/steer, fallback, and transcript state.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete already handled recent review and superseded-PR cleanup here, and the remaining question is product/runtime lifecycle direction rather than a narrow code ownership fix.
